I1.quote: Hydrogen adsorption measurements were performed on pristine graphene samples in a powder form using two volumetric systems.

I2.quote: The graphene sheets were prepared from artificial graphite using a chemical exfoliation method

I3.quote: A low gravimetric uptake (ca. 0.4 wt.%) is observed at 77 K under 100 kPa, which is decreased to 0.35 wt.% upon increasing temperature to 87 K.
I3.location: main, p. 2 (2330), Section 3 Results and discussion

I4.quote: BET analysis yields a relatively low specific surface area of 156 m2 g−1.
I4.location: main, p. 2 (2330), Section 3 Results and discussion

I5.quote: We evaluate the hydrogen adsorption behavior of the pristine single-layer graphene sheets in a powder form, which was performed at cryogenic and room temperatures.

notes: Technical Communication with original data (not a review). Volumetric H2 uptake on chemically exfoliated graphene powder: 77 K and 87 K up to 100 kPa (Fig. 2) and Sieverts at 290 K up to 6 MPa (<0.2 wt.%). BET area (N2, Fig. 1) measured on the same pristine graphene sample. Superscript minus in 'm2 g−1' confirmed on page image (text layer drops it). No retraction notice; no statement that the uptake data were published before.
